analysis:
Examined the GemmaCheck.swift base and head text and the QwenDecodeCheck.swift metadata and patch excerpt. Both files are in the darkbloom-cluster-tp-check developer and bench tool, not the provider serving path. They are outside TB-002 (coordinator WebSocket) and TB-011 (App Attest authorization), and no cache storage is touched, so T-041 is not engaged.

GemmaCheck.swift changes:
- A new --layer-stride option is validated as an integer in 0...64 (head lines 151-152). It is applied only when paged and when benchLayerStrideApplies(mode:) holds (lines 164-167).
- The value is added to the ranks' workload digest for the tp mode (line 207), so ranks that disagree on it fail closed before loading.
- Generation is wrapped in Gemma4TensorParallelModel.withLayerStride(layerStride) (lines 234-275), and the `generation` variable became an implicitly unwrapped optional. If the closure throws, the error propagates before `generation` is used, so there is no nil dereference.
- A decode step timing note is added (lines 276-280). It prints only the stride and step time statistics and no prompts, tokens or hosts. The existing 'report names roles and chips only' property is preserved.
- Sealed-bench keys remain explicitly labeled as an unauthenticated ephemeral exchange for benchmarking. Nothing in this PR promotes them to product use.

No findings. Remaining unverified items, which are outside the supplied evidence:
- QwenDecodeCheck.swift: only the patch excerpt was visible and it was truncated. It appears to enable --backend jaccl and add --layer-strides and --build-ahead options. Reviewers should check that the JACCL_* environment and hostfile handling does not log hosts or addresses into reports.
- Gemma4TensorParallelModel.withLayerStride: I could not see whether it mutates global state, or whether it could leak into the product path. Its implementation is in a file not supplied.

needs_deeper_review is set because of the truncated QwenDecodeCheck patch.
